question.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2\}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of $z={y}^{2}-{x}^{3}$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 2.$ What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z={y}^{2}-{x}^{3},\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2.
$$

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}-{x}^{3})=-3{x}^{2}, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}-{x}^{3})=2y,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(-3{x}^{2})}^{2}+{(2y)}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+9{x}^{4}+4{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is $\sqrt{1+9{x}^{4}+4{y}^{2}}.$
